key_concept: Sexual reproduction in fungi has three stages: plasmogamy (fusion of protoplasms), karyogamy (fusion of nuclei) and meiosis in the zygote, which produces haploid spores.
steps: A. Fusion of the protoplasms of two motile or non-motile gametes is called plasmogamy, so A matches II.
B. Fusion of the two nuclei is called karyogamy, so B matches III. In ascomycetes and basidiomycetes karyogamy is delayed, giving a dikaryotic stage ($n+n$).
C. The diploid ($2n$) zygote undergoes meiosis to form haploid ($n$) spores, so C matches I.
Combined match: A-II, B-III, C-I, which is option (1).
why_not_others: Option (2) gives B to meiosis, but meiosis halves chromosome number and does not fuse nuclei. Option (3) swaps plasmogamy and karyogamy. Option (4) wrongly links protoplasm fusion to meiosis and spore formation to plasmogamy.
common_trap: Students often swap plasmogamy and karyogamy; remember that 'plasma' refers to cytoplasm (protoplasm) and 'karyo' refers to the nucleus.
time_saving_tip: Once you see that A must be plasmogamy, only options (1) and (2) remain. Meiosis gives haploid spores, so C-I settles option (1).
